9. LONG TERM CONSEQUENCES OF PCOD:

-Incidence= 2.2 – 26%.
-More in South Asians.
-Commonest Endocrine problem in females.

Diagnosis:

•Rotterdam Criteria: 2 out of 3
•In adolescent :3 out of 3
⇨PCO on USG – 12 or more follicles or 2 – 9mm or ovarian volume >10ml3
⇨Oligo/anovulation
⇨Clinical/Biochemical hyperandrogenism
-Biochemical FAI
-Clinical hirsutism

(FAI=Total testosterone/SHBG x 100)

D/D of irregular cycles:

1.PCOD – diagnosis of exclusion
2.Hypothyroidism
3.Hyper – prolactinemia
4.Acromegaly
5.Obesity

Assessment of women with PCOS @ initial diagnosis:

•BMI + waist circumference
•CVD factors:
1.Smoking
2.Fx of type 2 DM.
3.Dyslipidemia
⇨Cholesterol.
⇨TG.
⇨HDL.
4.HTN
5.DM – type 2
6.Physical Activity.

Virilization:

•Deep voice , Breast size muscle bulk,

Clitoral Hypertrophy, rapidly progressing Hirsutism <1year duration.

D/D: of virilization

•CAH late onset.
•Cushing syndrome.
•Androgen secreting tumors.
•Acromegaly.

Testosterone >5 or Double than normal:

1: Androgen secreting tumors.

2: CAH

 

17 OH – progesterone diagnostic of CAH.

 

Borderline 17 OH – Progesterone diagnosis is Confirmed by

ACTH stimulation Test
